name: Cindy Lee
label: Realistik
lede: Patrick Flegel left Women after a brawl in Victoria, spent a decade making drag-pop records almost nobody could find, then put a 32-song album on YouTube and a Geocities page and watched Pitchfork crown it.

eras.title: Four friends, two records, 180 shows
eras.text: Women came out of Calgary with a debut recorded in a basement and a culvert, then a second record that critics still rank among the decade's best. The tour behind it ended in a fistfight.

years.src: Wikipedia: Women (band) · Stereogum: Women Brawl, Break Up?
years.h: Women form in Calgary: two brothers, a drummer, a guitarist
years.p: Patrick Flegel and Matt Flegel were joined by Mike Wallace and Chris Reimer. Flemish Eye's Ian Russell later called them friends since elementary school.
years.xp: Patrick played guitar and sang, Matt played bass and percussion, Wallace drums, Reimer guitar and samples. Both albums came out on Calgary's Flemish Eye in Canada and on Jagjaguwar in the US.

years.h: Women's debut, made in a basement, a culvert and a crawlspace
years.p: [[Patrick Flegel|35a5d8f3-e394-4f5e-9b11-2d1049e7827f]], his brother [[Matt Flegel|96c7a09f-bbd2-4b91-a91a-33a58ba417bb]], Chris Reimer and Mike Wallace cut it with [[Chad VanGaalen|d5c5c11b-153d-4f28-9525-db5ec1bfe0ad]] between December 2007 and February 2008. Pitchfork gave it 7.9.
years.xp:
VanGaalen recorded the album in his Calgary basement, an outdoor culvert and a crawlspace, with boom boxes and tape machines doing the work of a studio. Flemish Eye put it out in Canada and Jagjaguwar in the US. Pitchfork ranked "Black Rice" No. 18 among the best songs of 2008.

Wikipedia's count has the band playing more than 180 shows across North America and Europe over 2008 and 2009.

years.h: Public Strain: ten months at Yoko Eno for a colder, stranger record
years.p: VanGaalen produced again, at his own studio. Pitchfork gave it 8.0 and it made the 2011 Polaris longlist.
years.xp:
The band spent about ten months at VanGaalen's Yoko Eno studio in Calgary. Wikipedia lists the release date as August 23, 2010 while the band's own page gives September 28; we use the year only.

Closing track "Eyesore" is the one fans and critics point to first. Sputnikmusic later put the record third on its decade list.

years.src: Exclaim!: Women Implode Onstage in BC · Stereogum: Women Brawl, Break Up?
years.h: Lucky Bar, Victoria: the brothers fight, the set dissolves
years.p: A witness said Patrick Flegel threw punches at Matt Flegel during soundcheck. Onstage, Patrick told the room this was the last show.
years.xp:
According to Exclaim!, Patrick announced "we're breaking up right now, you're all going to see our last show." After about five songs Reimer and Matt left the stage, Wallace followed, and Patrick smashed Matt's guitar against an amp.

The label cancelled Vancouver, Ymir, Edmonton and a European tour. Flemish Eye head Ian Russell said the band needed a break after two months on the road and asked for privacy for what he called a close-knit group of friends since elementary school.

eras.title: A death, and a new name
eras.text: Women never played again. Reimer died, the Flegel brothers went separate ways, and Patrick began releasing music that would become Cindy Lee.

years.src: Exclaim!: Christopher Reimer's Cause of Death Revealed · Spin: Posthumous Collection by Late Women Guitarist Chris Reimer
years.h: Chris Reimer, Women's guitarist, dies at 26
years.p: The label said he died in his sleep of complications related to a heart condition. His funeral was in Calgary on February 29.
years.xp:
On the day of the funeral Women's labels ran a coordinated listening event, asking fans to play both albums back to back. His family set up a memorial fund.

Flemish Eye later released Hello People, a double LP of Reimer's four-track and phone-memo recordings compiled by friends and family, on April 19, 2018.

years.h: Matt Flegel and Mike Wallace start Viet Cong, later Preoccupations
years.p: With guitarists Scott Munro and Daniel Christiansen they formed the band in Calgary. Name criticism led to a rebrand in April 2016.
years.xp: Viet Cong put out its self-titled album in 2015, had a show at Oberlin College cancelled over the name in March 2015, and became [[Preoccupations|9ee1988d-66ec-4c29-98d6-876a45e0fcbd]] in 2016.

years.src: Wikipedia: Cindy Lee (band) · Kool Kids Music Club
years.h: Flegel and Morgan Cook record the Nightstalker EP as Androgynous Mind
years.p: The duo is where the Cindy Lee project comes from, per Wikipedia. On Boxing Day, Tatlashea appeared on Isolated Now Waves.
years.xp: Wikipedia lists Tatlashea as a Boxing Day 2012 release, reissued in 2016. Early Cindy Lee records came out in tiny runs and on small labels, which is part of why the project stayed under the radar for a decade.

eras.title: A drag act nobody could find
eras.text: Flegel kept releasing records under the Cindy Lee name through small labels, cassette runs and split singles, performing in drag over recorded backing.

years.h: Split single with Red Mass, "Holding the Devil's Hand"
years.p: It came out on Mongrel Zine, one of the project's first releases after Women.

years.src: The FADER: Patrick Flegel on creating the haunted pop universe of Cindy Lee · Wikipedia: Cindy Lee (band)
years.h: Act of Tenderness gives Cindy Lee its first real album
years.p: CCQSK released it in 2015. Maple Death and W.25th reissued it in 2018. The FADER dates Cindy Lee's emergence to this record.
years.xp:
The FADER describes Flegel's drawing on the suburban closet-queen figure and on Faye Dunaway, Patsy Cline and Akihiro Miwa. Both 2015 albums were reissued in 2018 by Maple Death and W.25th.

In 2015 Flegel also toured as a live member of [[Freak Heat Waves|7197c548-ec59-4e59-80ef-56901a80e1ef]].

years.h: Malenkost arrives the same year, on Isolated Now Waves
years.p: One of two Cindy Lee albums in 2015. Force Exposure's catalog describes Brill Building hooks next to No Wave noise.

years.src: Spin: Posthumous Collection by Late Women Guitarist Chris Reimer
years.h: Hello People: Chris Reimer's own recordings, on two LPs
years.p: Flemish Eye released a double LP of his four-track projects and phone memos, compiled by friends and family.

years.h: Model Express goes out as 100 gold cassettes
years.p: The compilation came out on CCQSK. W.25th pressed it to vinyl in 2020.

eras.title: Karen Carpenter and the lathe cuts
eras.text: Cindy Lee signed to a real label, got a Polaris longlist nod, then vanished into tiny editions again.

years.src: Wikipedia: What's Tonight to Eternity? · The FADER: Patrick Flegel on creating the haunted pop universe of Cindy Lee
years.h: What's Tonight to Eternity? turns Karen Carpenter into a horror-pop record
years.p: W.25th released it on Valentine's Day 2020. Pitchfork gave it 7.1 and it made the Polaris longlist.
years.xp:
Flegel told The FADER about compiling a two-and-a-half-hour personal biography of Carpenter, whose overwork and the people feeding on her career resonated with Flegel's own mental health during the Women touring years.

Exclaim! gave it 9/10 and Paste 8.4. Andrew Flegel played drums. Flegel recorded almost all of it alone at Realistik Studios.

years.src: Force Exposure: Cindy Lee · Wikipedia: Cindy Lee (band)
years.h: Cat o' Nine Tails appears in an edition of 50
years.p: Realistik pressed 50 lathe-cut copies, per Force Exposure. Isolated Now Waves gave it a wider release in 2023.
years.xp: Force Exposure lists it as originally 50 lathe-cut copies, combining classic songwriting with classical composition.

years.h: Pitchfork gives What's Tonight to Eternity? a 7.1; Polaris longlists it
years.p: Exclaim! gave it 9/10 and Paste 8.4. The album did not reach the Polaris shortlist.

years.src: Wikipedia: Cindy Lee (band) · Jacksonville Music Experience: Cindy Lee interview
years.h: "In a Moment Divine": Cindy Lee and Freak Heat Waves make a disco track
years.p: The single came out on Mood Hut. Freak Heat Waves members Steven Lind and Thomas Di Ninno reshaped an Amanda Lear-inspired original.
years.xp: Freak Heat Waves became Cindy Lee's closest allies. Lind co-wrote "Baby Blue" on Diamond Jubilee and mixed it, and the band opened the 2024 tour.

eras.title: Thirty-two songs and a Geocities page
eras.text: A double album appears on YouTube and a site built like 1998. A week of word-of-mouth later, Pitchfork gives it a 9.1.

years.src: NPR: How Cindy Lee became · Talkhouse: Not Lost in the Shuffle Again · Uproxx: Why Cindy Lee's Diamond Jubilee
years.h: Diamond Jubilee goes up on YouTube and a Geocities-style site
years.p: Thirty-two songs, two hours, no Spotify. Flegel suggested a $30 Canadian donation for the WAV download.
years.xp:
The album lived on a single two-hour YouTube video and on the Realistik Studios site. NPR quoted the site's line about Spotify's chief executive: "THE CEO OF SPOTIFY IS A THIEF AND A WAR PIG." Flegel is quoted by NPR saying, "I'd much rather bet on myself."

Flegel played nearly every part on digital 8-track, with synths from Steven Lind of [[Freak Heat Waves|7197c548-ec59-4e59-80ef-56901a80e1ef]]. Talkhouse called it a turn toward warmth and accessibility after six darker records, drawing on girl groups, reggae and Thin Lizzy-style guitar harmonies.

years.big: No Spotify. No press release. A 9.1.
years.src: Album of the Year: Diamond Jubilee · Wikipedia: Diamond Jubilee (album) · Paste: Diamond Jubilee review
years.h: Pitchfork's 9.1 is its highest score in four years
years.p: The review ran weeks after release, for a record with zero promotion. Paste gave it 9.2 and Metacritic averaged 91.
years.xp:
According to Wikipedia, it was Pitchfork's highest new-album rating since Fiona Apple's 2020 release. Reviewer Andy Cush called it "an essential trove of music" and each song "a foggy transmission from a rock 'n' roll netherworld."

The album went to No. 1 on RateYourMusic and on year-end lists at Exclaim!, Gorilla vs. Bear and Beats Per Minute.

years.src: Uproxx: Why Cindy Lee's Diamond Jubilee · NPR: How Cindy Lee became
years.h: The Diamond Jubilee tour starts, with Freak Heat Waves opening
years.p: Flegel played in drag over backing tracks: sequin dress, fur coat, blue wig, falsetto.
years.xp: Uproxx described the stage show as full theatrical drag over pre-recorded tracks. NPR reviewed the May 3 show at Cactus Club in Milwaukee: a 45-minute set on a cherry Telecaster.

years.src: Exclaim!: Cindy Lee Cancels the Remainder of 2024 Tour · NPR: How Cindy Lee became
years.h: Cindy Lee cancels the tour, hours before a Chicago show
years.p: About 12 dates, including Toronto and Montreal, were dropped. Venue Tubby's said "personal reasons"; Freak Heat Waves said it was beyond their control.
years.xp: Exclaim! reported the cancellation on May 5. No statement came from Flegel. The Chicago show was cancelled at the last minute; Milwaukee on May 3 was the final performance of the run.

years.h: Flegel teams with Panda Bear and Moon Diagrams
years.p: The "Defense" single with Noah Lennox of Animal Collective, and Cemetery Classics with Deerhunter's Moses Archuleta, both came out in 2024.

years.h: Diamond Jubilee makes the Polaris Music Prize shortlist
years.p: The Canadian prize shortlisted an album whose only homes were YouTube and a self-hosted website.

years.h: Bandcamp and physical editions arrive
years.p: Cindy Lee moved the catalog to Bandcamp. Superior Viaduct's W.25th imprint issued the album on triple LP and double CD.

eras.title: Back on stage, for now
eras.text: Pitchfork's No. 1 album of the year, then Pitchfork's No. 3 album of the 2020s so far, and a few big rooms.

years.src: Wikipedia: Diamond Jubilee (album) · Album of the Year: Diamond Jubilee
years.h: Pitchfork names Diamond Jubilee its No. 1 album of 2024
years.p: Pitchfork ranked it ahead of the rest of its 50 best albums of the year. Exclaim! and Gorilla vs. Bear also picked it first.
years.xp: Pitchfork later ranked the album third on its best albums of the 2020s so far, per Wikipedia.

years.src: Stereogum: Cindy Lee Announces First Concerts · Paste: Diamond Jubilee review
years.h: Four shows in bigger rooms: Chicago, Toronto, Montreal, Brooklyn
years.p: Empty Bottle on November 5, Massey Hall on November 6, Rialto Theatre on November 10 and Brooklyn Paramount on November 15, with Freak Heat Waves on three.
years.xp: Stereogum announced the dates as the first since the curtailed spring tour. Flegel had hinted the run might be Cindy Lee's last American tour.
